python_unchanged.rule: A request without target, or with target python, returns the same bytes as the accepted compiler-v1 default for the same request. No existing CNL text, typed prompt, bundle, asset or Python output changes.
checks: All 127 public Python products are byte-identical to their accepted outputs.
All 544 historical jobs keep their accepted results.
The legacy 100 and 214 case sets keep their scope.
Every negative case python_control_body gives its python_control_expected result (tests/rust-output-v1/check_python_controls.py).
Every coverage case gives the same Python bundle payload_sha256 and Python file hashes as the frozen evidence (tests/rust-output-v1/validate_cases.py).

target_selection_checks: Every target-examples.json body gives its expected result.
Every RT case gives exactly its expected diagnostic, located in the raw request body.
A target python request gives the same bytes as the request without target, for every acceptance case and every CNL positive fixture.
The CLI forwards --target unchanged and exits with status 2 on a refusal.
scope_checks: Every RS and RP case gives exactly its expected diagnostic with target rust.
Every out-of-scope public example, CNL positive fixture and legacy job gives UNSUPPORTED_TARGET with the refusal case-inventory.json records for it, with target rust.
The compiler refusal for each case equals tests/rust-output-v1/rust_profile.py on the typed prompt.
bundle_checks: For every acceptance case, the CNL and typed JSON requests with target rust return byte-identical som.dsl-bundle.v2 bundles.
Every Rust bundle validates against bundle.schema.json, has at most 12 files and 64 blocks, and every block id starts with rust.
Two compiles and two assembles of the same request give the same bytes.
The assembled files are exactly the product-layout.json file set, and Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock equal the reference files.

assemble_refusals.base: A valid Rust bundle for the acceptance case example-v1, and for A6 the bundle for example-v5.
assemble_refusals.rehash: Unless a recipe says otherwise, recompute prompt_sha256, dsl_sha256 and payload_sha256 with the frozen formulas after the change, so the hash check passes and the named check is reached.
assemble_refusals.span: Line, column and byte spans locate the pointer target in the canonical assemble request body, computed at test time.

each_acceptance_case: cargo test --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1 with TEST_DATABASE_URL on a fresh database; a missing database is a failure
schema equivalence with the Python migration for the same prompt (behavior-normalization.json)
the behavior parity suite against the Python product for the same prompt, after the frozen normalization
the strict refusals in behavior-normalization.json divergences D1 to D5 checked on the Rust product alone
product_gates.no_sampling: Every acceptance case runs every gate. A missing result, a failure and a skipped check are each reported as such and block acceptance.

issue_gates.#46: The behavior suite and harness pass on the current Python products for every acceptance case before any Rust product exists.
issue_gates.#47: target_selection_checks, scope_checks and python_unchanged pass. Rust compiles may still return a not-yet-implemented diagnostic for in-scope prompts only until #48.
issue_gates.#48: bundle_checks, assemble_refusals and product_gates pass for every v1 to v4 acceptance case.
issue_gates.#49: bundle_checks, assemble_refusals and product_gates pass for every v5 acceptance case.
issue_gates.#50: Every check in this plan passes on one recorded build, with the evidence hashed.
issue_gates.#51: A qualified switch on a QA port, a canary and a rollback check pass before the default on 8765 changes.

phase2.rule: The sections above stay the phase 1 plan and gates (#46 to #51). This section is the phase 2 plan (#53 to #56). python_unchanged and target_selection_checks apply unchanged. For phase 2, refusals replaces the phase 1 scope_checks and the expected UNSUPPORTED_TARGET results of the RS rows of negative-cases.json, which stay the phase 1 record. RP01 to RP03 still run and keep their compiler-v1 diagnostics. Every phase 2 check runs on every case it names: there is no sampling, and a missing result, a failure and a skipped check each block acceptance.

cases.phase2: Every row of phase2/case-inventory.json (584): 444 legacy v6 and v7 jobs, 115 CNL positive fixtures, 3 public examples and RS01 to RS22.
cases.legacy: The 544 legacy jobs of legacy544 run-005: the 100 of case-inventory.json and the 444 of phase2/case-inventory.json.

phase2.refusals: With target rust, the only UNSUPPORTED_TARGET results for these cases are RS12 (its CNL form) and RS13 (its JSON form), with exactly the query_parameter_collision diagnostic tests/rust-output-v1/rust_profile_phase2.py gives for the typed prompt. Any other UNSUPPORTED_TARGET, and any NOT_IMPLEMENTED or OUTPUT_QUALITY_FAILED result, fails acceptance.
phase2.phase1_unchanged: For every phase 1 acceptance case, the Rust bundle differs from the accepted phase 1 bundle (rust-output-050) only in the Rust asset descriptors and the hashes over them, and the assembled files are byte-identical.
bundle_checks: For every phase 2 product case, the CNL and typed JSON requests with target rust return byte-identical som.dsl-bundle.v2 bundles; a case with one form runs that form.
Every Rust bundle validates against bundle.schema.json, has at most 12 files and 64 blocks per file, and every block id starts with rust.
Two compiles and two assembles of the same request give the same bytes.
The assembled files are exactly the file set of the product-layout.json phase2 shape the prompt selects, and Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock equal the reference files of that shape.

assemble_refusals.rule: assemble_refusals above run unchanged on the example-v1 base, except A6 and A8, which phase 2 replaces as below. A1, A2, A4, A5, A7 and A9 also run on the PUBLIC_v6 Rust bundle as base, with the same code, status and pointer.
assemble_refusals.A6: Replace the prompt with the RS12 typed prompt. Recompute the shared compiler-v1 descriptors for it, keep the Rust descriptors and the Rust DSL, and rehash. Result: UNSUPPORTED_TARGET 422, with the prompt_pointer of rust_profile_phase2.py under /bundle/prompt.
assemble_refusals.A8: The A8 change gives 200, and the files equal the compile and assemble of the renamed prompt with target rust: Title is a field with an R2 Rust name and the wire name Title.

product_gates: cargo build --locked --offline, with CARGO_HOME holding only the vendored union of toolchain.json phase2_crates vendor

cargo test --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1 on a fresh database: TEST_DATABASE_URL for PostgreSQL shapes, MONGODB_URL with SOM_TEST_DATABASE_NAME for MongoDB shapes; a missing setting is a failure
PostgreSQL shapes: schema equivalence with the Python migration for the same prompt, as phase 1, ignoring _som_rust_migrations and alembic_version
MongoDB shapes: after som_app migrate upgrade, the collections and indexes (keys, order and uniqueness; names not compared) equal the Python product's after its migrate upgrade
the phase 2 behavior suite: som-rs/behavior/phase2/check_phase2.py run --language rust passes the case's checker (phase2/case-inventory.json) with no assembled file changed
the same case passes check_phase2.py --language python, or is a Python defect or phase 2 refusal that phase2/behavior.json explains
phase2.legacy_gate: Every one of the 544 legacy jobs gives a Rust product that passes product_gates (phase 1 jobs: the phase 1 product_gates and parity), and its Python result stays the accepted one.

issue_gates.#53: bundle_checks, product_gates and refusals pass for every case whose constructs.json owner is #53: v5 with capabilities, v6, and the naming refusal removals (RS cases). phase1_unchanged passes.
issue_gates.#54: bundle_checks and product_gates pass for every v7 case, with flow_fault_checks and flow_provider_fault_checks and a fault injected at every step that has undo.
issue_gates.#55: Every check of this section and python_unchanged passes on one recorded candidate build, with every case receipt kept, and an independent audit (som-rs/scripts/rust_output_acceptance/audit/audit055.py), written from this plan and the raw outputs only, reports no failure and nothing unrun.
issue_gates.#56: A qualified switch on a QA port, Rust canaries on the local emulators (example-v1, example-v5, a v6 PostgreSQL product, a v6 MongoDB product, a v7 flow with undo), the Python canaries and a rollback to the phase 1 default pass before the default on 8765 changes, and the change has the user's explicit approval.

amendments: After the freeze receipt is sealed, a change to any frozen file is a numbered amendment with its reason, the old and new hashes, and an independent review.
